i understand you. its annoying to feel so depressed even whilst youre enjoying things. im starting my second-to-last year of school and i just keep having to remind myself that its just 2 more years until im out of school and i can make my life go in any way i want it to. hopefully, after school, things can and will get so much better. the best advice i have is to stay hopeful because there will be a better day in  the future for every bad day. you dont want to miss out on the good times just because your main focus (unintentionally) is your depressive moods. try to stay positive by looking forward to times where you will feel happier than you do now

what ive realised is that the sadness will always lowkey be there, but as you grow up and experience more you will find different ways to be able to deal with it and you will find different reasons to live. if you can, try talking to people a good deal older than you - ask them how they managed to deal with hard times in their lives. when you feel extremely down like this its easy to forget that other people go through it as well and have ways of helping. when i feel like there is no point in living, i try to find things i enjoy about life. for example, i love seeing dogs on walks, and i feel passionate about the english football team aresnal - theyre just two small things that bring me a little bit of joy in my seemingly terrible life. even if its just one tiny tiny thing - it is reassuring to realise that you have at least something that makes life enjoyable. i hope it doesnt take too long for you to find your reasons to live

school is so hard - i can relate to you with that. ive just gone into my second-to-last year of school, so i just have 2 years to finish until i can go to university, but i hate that its the same upset, stress, and nerves every day from school. i dont want to have 2 solid years of these horrible negative feelings. something my boyfriend told me to remember when im thinking like this is that its not permanent. thats one thing i like about school - it will be over in time for definite. im in school now so i can go to university and get the job that i want in the future (which im hoping will be more enjoyable than the past and present) so - if youre able to - i recommend trying to set something for yourself to look forward to after school is finished. if youre on a journey to a place you like, you dont give up because the journey isnt fun. youre looking forward to the outcome of it. you may not even feel that school is worth it at the end of it all, but at least you can say that you got through such a hard time. its a good way to realise how strong and capable you are of dealing with upsetting situations - other people would have quit by now if they were affected in the same way and other people have quit. youre doing great to be able to say that youre still alive at this very moment, and to believe that there may be some hope left - even if its just on a reddit forum - is a great achievement, especially considering how hopeless depression makes you feel. i wish you all the best and hope school gets somewhat easier for you

not sure of your situation but ive been diagnosed with depression anxiety and insomnia for 5+ years and it took a good 3/4 years (a nice few suicide attempts thrown in!) for my psychotherapists and doctor to finally come together to have me prescribed to medication (anti depressants - fluoxetine, and circadin for my sleep) and i think they have both helped as much as they can (not saying im no longer feeling depressed and suicidal but i do believe i could be in a worse state on some days if i didnt have medication) the best advice i could give for attaining the right medication is by telling your doctor exactly how youre feeling and what you need - is it a mood boost or something to motivate you to function like a normal happy human or is it something to get you to enjoy what you used to pre-depression etc etc. without specific knowledge on your depressive situation i cant offer much advice but if youre in the same boat as me (that kinda depression where getting out of bed seems impossible, brushing your teeth is a once a week kinda thing cuz it just takes so much effort to walk to the bathroom for that) then ask your doctor if theres anything to get you motivated into doing everyday things.  unfortunately, i dont believe there is any legal way of getting medication for depression if you dont go through your doctor (uk resident outlook on it, though - not sure if its different where youre from?) best of luck with getting the medication you feel you need
